question: If the price of a product is first increased by 18% and then decreased by 22%. Find the percentage change in the price (correct to two places of decimals).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net % change = a + b + ab/100 where a = +18, b = −22

= 18 + (−22) + (18 × −22)/100

= 18 − 22 − 396/100

= −4 − 3.96 = −7.96%

Negative sign means decrease.

**∴ The correct answer is 7.96% decrease.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First change = +18% (increase)

Second change = −22% (decrease)

**Formula used:**

Net % change = a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100

Where a = first % change | b = second % change

Use + for increase and − for decrease.

 Original ₹100 
• +18% After +18% ₹118 
• −22% After −22% ₹92.04 
• 
• 
• Net change = 92.04 − 100 = −7.96% a + b + ab/100 = 18 − 22 − 3.96 = −7.96% Decrease of 7.96% 
 
 

**Calculations:**

Let original price = ₹100

⇒ After 18% increase = 100 × 118/100 = ₹118

⇒ After 22% decrease on ₹118 = 118 × 78/100 = ₹92.04

⇒ Net change = 92.04 − 100 = −7.96

⇒ % change = −7.96%

Using direct formula: a + b + ab/100 = 18 + (−22) + (18 × −22)/100

⇒ = 18 − 22 − 396/100

⇒ = −4 − 3.96

⇒ = −7.96%

Since value is negative ⇒ it is a decrease.

**∴ The correct answer is 7.96% decrease.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change — Direct Formula

For two successive % changes a and b: Net % = a + b + ab/100. Use + for increase and − for decrease. Example: +20% then −20% ⇒ net = 20 − 20 + (20 × −20)/100 = −4% — always results in a net decrease when same % is applied both ways.

Multiplying Factor Method

x% increase → multiply by (100+x)/100 | x% decrease → multiply by (100−x)/100. For this question: 100 × 118/100 × 78/100 = 92.04. Net factor = 0.9204 ⇒ decrease of 7.96%. This method works for any number of successive changes.

Three Successive % Changes

For three changes a, b, c: apply the formula twice. First find net of a and b ⇒ then apply formula again with c. Or use multiplying factor method directly: Original × (1±a/100) × (1±b/100) × (1±c/100). This is the fastest method for three or more changes.

% Increase Needed to Recover After Decrease

If price drops by x%, the % increase needed to recover = x/(100−x) × 100. For this question final price is 92.04% of original — to recover: 7.96/92.04 × 100 ≈ 8.65% increase is needed. Recovery % is always greater than the decrease %.
